rules.description: Assignments must never contain Markdown code fences or inline backticks—return raw strings or placeholders only.
Every node and edge must use a UUID-formatted id.
Introduce variables with assign steps before referencing them in endpoints or messages.
Every variable created in an assign step must be referenced by a later node (endpoint params, conditions, transforms, or messages); remove unused values.
Only include `multiChoiceQuestion`, `dynamicChoices`, and button payload metadata when the service brief requires interactive choices; omit empty scaffolding.
Attach `endpoint` objects only to the node that actually performs the API call; later assign or message nodes must reference the prior response instead of embedding endpoint metadata again.
Do not wrap `${...}` expressions inside other `${...}` segments or strings that already contain substitutions; each placeholder must be standalone.
Avoid nesting `${...}` inside other placeholders; use literal variable names when indexing (e.g., `${data.items[indexVar]}` instead of `${data.items[${indexVar}]}`).

Condition rules may only use standard JavaScript comparison operators (`==`, `===`, `!=`, `!==`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`). Compute any other logic in an earlier assign step and reference the resulting variable.
Provide explicit labels on edges leaving condition nodes.
Reference endpoint responses using `${<endpointName>_res...}` where `<endpointName>` matches the `endpoint.name`; do not invent custom aliases.
Endpoint steps are optional; include only when external data is required.
Client-facing textfield steps should appear after data preparation is complete.

output.notes: Return a single JSON object representing the service graph.
